Maintenance Report — MNT-0177-002

Asset: WELL-0177 (NE-08 Well 177, T200, Northeast Block 8) Equipment: flowline Work started: 06 Jan 2023 08:00 · Finished: 07 Jan 2023 02:00 · Well stopped for this job: 18 hours Crew lead: Kevin Price (U-303) · Crew: Brian Coleman Triggered by: inspection INS-0177-0012 on 2023-01-05 Report written: 09 Jan 2023

What happened

The weekly drone inspection INS-0177-0012 at 10:30 on 2023-01-05 found crude oil on the pad: about 8.1% of the pad area, estimated 4.5 bbl. The inspector noted: "Pooled fluid near flowline." The field operator shut the well in, closed the flowline valve and placed earth berms and absorbent pads. The release was contained about 5.8 hours after the inspection. The crew traced the leak to a threaded coupling on the flowline close to the wellhead.

Root cause

Corrosion under a failed protective wrap on the coupling.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started, but it was not written down (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 0 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).
  • Hot work permit issued for welding; gas test before welding read 3% LEL, below the 10% limit (WS-04).

Work done

  1. Excavated around the coupling.
  2. Cut out the failed coupling and the pipe ends.
  3. Welded in new pipe and a new fitting.
  4. Coated the new joints.
  5. Excavated the stained soil.
  6. Backfilled after the pressure test.

Summary of the fix: replaced leaking flowline section and remediated soil.

Testing and return to service

Pressure-tested the repaired section at 281 psi (1.25 × the flowline's maximum operating pressure of 225 psi) and held it for 4 hours with no pressure drop (WS-05). The well was returned to production.

Spill clean-up and waste

  • About 2.8 m³ of stained soil excavated, bagged and sent to an approved disposal site under waste manifest WM-0177-002 (WS-06).
  • 2 soil samples taken around the spill; the highest result after clean-up was 0.26% TPH, below the 1.0% target (SR-03).

maintenance.action: Replaced the electric motor with an exchange unit
maintenance.report_html:
Maintenance Report — MNT-0177-017

Asset: WELL-0177 (NE-08 Well 177, T200, Northeast Block 8) Equipment: pump jack Work started: 03 May 2025 08:00 · Finished: 06 May 2025 01:00 · Well stopped for this job: 65 hours Crew lead: Daniel Foster (U-302) · Crew: Kevin Price Triggered by: inspection INS-0177-0129 on 2025-05-01 Report written: 06 May 2025

What happened

Field staff reported that the motor breaker kept tripping and the pump jack would not run. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0177-0129 showed the wellhead at 28.4 °C with the air at 27.3 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. An insulation test showed a winding fault, so the motor was replaced with an exchange unit.

Root cause

Moisture got into the motor terminal box and damaged the windings.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 1 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Disconnected and removed the motor.
  2. Fitted the exchange motor on the existing base.
  3. Aligned the sheaves and tensioned the belts.
  4. Checked rotation direction and motor current.

Summary of the fix: replaced the electric motor with an exchange unit.

Testing and return to service

Ran the unit for 2 hours; motor current within the nameplate rating and stroke rate normal. The well was returned to production.

Maintenance Report — MNT-0177-025

Asset: WELL-0177 (NE-08 Well 177, T200, Northeast Block 8) Equipment: pump jack Work started: 30 Jan 2026 08:00 · Finished: 04 Feb 2026 14:00 · Well stopped for this job: 126 hours Crew lead: Kevin Price (U-303) · Crew: Brian Coleman Triggered by: inspection INS-0177-0167 on 2026-01-29 Report written: 04 Feb 2026

What happened

Field staff reported that the pumper heard grinding from the walking beam and saw the horsehead wobbling. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0177-0167 showed the wellhead at 6.0 °C with the air at 6.7 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. A vibration check and visual inspection found play in the saddle bearing and scoring on the bearing housing. The well stayed shut in for about 3 days longer than the repair itself because heavy rain made the lease road impassable for the service truck.

Root cause

Bearing wear from long service and an overdue grease interval.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 2 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Lowered the horsehead and supported the walking beam with a crane.
  2. Removed the saddle bearing assembly.
  3. Cleaned the housing and checked alignment.
  4. Fitted a new saddle bearing and torqued the bolts to the manufacturer's values.
  5. Greased all structural bearings.

Summary of the fix: replaced saddle bearing and re-greased.

Testing and return to service

Ran the unit for 2 hours: smooth stroke, no knocking, bearing temperature normal. The well was returned to production.

  • Check saddle bearings on neighbouring units of the same age.
